grammars.text:
# find — predicate-expression grammar.
#
# Input shape: the encoder in `./encoder.ts` takes the shell's
# tokenized args + the `_meta` channel and produces a single string
# where:
#   - Structural tokens (keywords, operators, terminators, grouping)
#     are bare and whitespace-separated.
#   - Every value is either a bareword (if its source was a single
#     bareword wordPart) or a double-quoted token (if the source had
#     a quoted / expansion / brace-list part).
#   - Inside `-exec ... ;` / `-exec ... +` the encoder always quotes
#     args (even barewords), so the only bare tokens between -exec
#     and its terminator are the terminator itself.
#
# Structure: the grammar produces a FLAT LIST of items (atoms +
# `-o` markers + `-a`/`-and` no-op markers). The visitor groups
# items by `-o` boundaries, ANDs items within each group, and ORs
# the groups together. This avoids left-recursive infix grammar
# and keeps the cpat side small.
#
# Precedence (visitor):
#   - `-not` / `!` (prefix on a single atom — handled in `notExpr`)
#   - implicit AND between adjacent atoms (visitor combines)
#   - `-o` / `-or` (lowest — visitor splits chain on these)

# ─── Whitespace ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ws = /[ \t\n\r]+/

# ─── Tokens ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Standard double-quoted string. Visitor unescapes `\\` and `\"`.
quoted = /"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"/

# A bareword is any non-whitespace, non-quote, non-paren run. Listed
# AFTER the keyword rules in alternations so cpat tries the keyword
# literals first and `bareword` is the fallback for everything else.
# Includes `;` and `+` so a value like `foo+bar` parses as one token
# — `-exec` terminator disambiguation is handled by the encoder
# always quoting exec args.
bareword = /[^"\s()]+/

# ─── Structural single-char tokens ──────────────────────────
openParen  = "("
closeParen = ")"
semi       = ";"
plus       = "+"

# ─── Operator keywords ──────────────────────────────────────
notKw  = "-not"
bangKw = "!"
notOp  = notKw | bangKw

andKw  = "-and"
aKw    = "-a"
andOp  = andKw | aKw

orKw   = "-or"
oKw    = "-o"
orOp   = orKw | oKw

# ─── Predicate keywords ─────────────────────────────────────
maxdepthKw = "-maxdepth"
mindepthKw = "-mindepth"
typeKw     = "-type"
nameKw     = "-name"
inameKw    = "-iname"
pathKw     = "-path"
ipathKw    = "-ipath"
regexKw    = "-regex"
iregexKw   = "-iregex"
sizeKw     = "-size"
emptyKw    = "-empty"

# ─── Action keywords ────────────────────────────────────────
printKw  = "-print"
print0Kw = "-print0"
deleteKw = "-delete"
execKw   = "-exec"

# ─── Value (predicate argument) ─────────────────────────────
# Accepts a quoted token OR a bareword. The encoder guarantees that
# values originating from quoted / expansion / brace-list parts arrive
# as `quoted`, so a value that happens to spell a keyword is
# unambiguous — the grammar isn't in keyword-position here.
value = quoted | bareword

# ─── Predicates ─────────────────────────────────────────────
pMaxdepth = maxdepthKw + ws + value
pMindepth = mindepthKw + ws + value
pType     = typeKw     + ws + value
pName     = nameKw     + ws + value
pIname    = inameKw    + ws + value
pPath     = pathKw     + ws + value
pIpath    = ipathKw    + ws + value
pRegex    = regexKw    + ws + value
pIregex   = iregexKw   + ws + value
pSize     = sizeKw     + ws + value
pEmpty    = emptyKw

predicate = pMaxdepth
          | pMindepth
          | pType
          | pName
          | pIname
          | pPath
          | pIpath
          | pRegex
          | pIregex
          | pSize
          | pEmpty

# ─── Actions ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# -exec collects (quoted)+ until a bare `;` or `+`. The encoder
# always quotes -exec args, so the only bareword between -exec and
# the terminator is the terminator itself.
execArg     = quoted
execArgList = (execArg, ws trim)+
execTerm    = semi | plus
aExec       = execKw + ws + execArgList + ws + execTerm

aPrint  = printKw
aPrint0 = print0Kw
aDelete = deleteKw

action = aExec | aPrint0 | aDelete | aPrint

# ─── Grouping ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# `( ... )` wraps an inner chainItems list so precedence can be
# overridden. The visitor descends transparently into the group's
# inner chain.
group = openParen + ws? + chainItems + ws? + closeParen

# ─── Negation ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# `-not` / `!` is a prefix that binds to a single atom (the atom
# rule includes notExpr so `-not -not -name foo` works via right
# recursion).
notExpr = notOp + ws + atom

# ─── Atom ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
atom = group | notExpr | action | predicate

# ─── Chain items ────────────────────────────────────────────
# The visitor reads this list, splits on orMarker, AND-joins atoms
# within each segment, OR-joins segments. andMarker is consumed by
# the grammar (so `-a` / `-and` parse cleanly) but contributes no
# semantics — implicit AND is the default between atoms.
orMarker  = orOp
andMarker = andOp
chainItem = orMarker | andMarker | atom

chainItems = (chainItem, ws trim)+

# ─── Top level ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# pathArg is handled by `src/tools/find.ts` BEFORE encoding — it
# peels off the leading non-keyword positional and only the
# expression body is fed to cpat. So findExpr here is just an
# optional chainItems wrapped in optional whitespace.
findExpr = ws? + chainItems? + ws?
